title: Pages from the School Magazine
paragraphs: The school magazine had room for one more feature. Instead of choosing a single dramatic adventure, its editors gathered several brief accounts around a shared theme. They hoped readers would compare the situations and think about the reasons behind each action.

The opening pages introduced several situations worth examining carefully. The volunteers brought food to families in a desperate plight after the flood. Losing both the map and the phone left the hikers in a predicament. The scientist checked every measurement with great rigor. A dearth of rainfall left the reservoirs nearly empty.

The remaining pages widened the discussion with additional observations. Missing costumes and forgotten lines turned the opening night into a debacle. The picnic became a fiasco when the food spoiled and the tent collapsed. A brief computer glitch prevented us from saving the file. Calling the guest by the wrong name was an unfortunate gaffe.

When the group returned to its original question, the discussion had become more precise. The members could point to particular actions and details instead of relying on a vague impression. They did not force every account to teach the same lesson. Their final display invited readers to compare the evidence, explain a connection, and consider where that connection ended.

targets.definition: an awkward situation that is hard to escape
a serious lack of something needed
a complete and often embarrassing failure
an event that ends in a ridiculous or humiliating failure
a small technical problem or temporary fault
